claim: Enum formatters use the inverse target-framework condition from every other template. Consequently, on modern targets such as net8.0 the enum formatter's ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute is inactive, so not all generated code is decorated. On NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK it is instead active even though the change identifies those as targets where the attribute is unavailable, breaking the supported-target compilation criterion there.

claim: The enum formatter's preprocessor condition is inverted. On modern targets, including .NET 8, the generated EnumFormatter has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute, while NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK are the only targets where the attribute is emitted. This misses enum formatters in the requested coverage and risks using the attribute on precisely the legacy targets for which every other template suppresses it.

claim: Applying ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally to the generated partial resolver causes CS0579 when the consumer has already applied the same attribute to their partial resolver declaration. Attributes from partial declarations are combined, and ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiples, so existing user workarounds become compile errors.

This breaks enum formatter coverage exclusion on modern targets and can make generated enum formatters fail to compile on the older targets.
